records.scope: Classical probability-space/null-set background needed to state effective tests; computable measures; effective open sets; integral-test formulations.
records.why_it_matters: Test-based randomness definitions depend on exactly which null sets/measures/tests are effectively present.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Classical measure-theory foundations were not separately catalogued in P1-S001; only randomness-relevant effective-measure machinery was started.
next_actions: Acquire authoritative effective-measure references and normalize conventions for effective openness, computable measures and integral tests.

records.area: Historical statistical randomness, normality, von Mises and Church selection
records.scope: Normal numbers/statistical frequency tests; collectives; admissible place selections; Church effectivization; later stochasticity terminology.
records.why_it_matters: Separates frequency/selection approaches from stronger effective-test and betting notions and prevents ahistorical equivalence claims.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Borel and von Mises original sources not yet catalogued directly; Church source statement inspected; later terminology crosswalk incomplete.
next_actions: Add primary Borel/von Mises records and source-supported relationships among normality, Church stochasticity and modern notions.

records.area: Martin-Löf randomness and effective null tests
records.scope: Core definitions, universal tests, equivalent formulations and foundational history for individual infinite sequences.
records.why_it_matters: Central benchmark notion against which many weaker, stronger, relative and generalized notions are calibrated.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Original 1966 paper abstract inspected but its internal theorem statements/proofs were not yet fully indexed.
next_actions: Inspect original statements and add Solovay-test, martingale and further complexity characterizations with primary sources.

records.area: Schnorr, computable, Kurtz and weak randomness notions
records.scope: Major weaker notions; exact test/betting resources; strictness and separation theorems; weak-n hierarchy where relevant.
records.why_it_matters: These notions expose how changes in effectivity/resource constraints alter randomness and provide a calibrated local landscape around Martin-Löf randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Exact original Schnorr source not yet statement-inspected.
Kurtz thesis/source metadata was located during searching but no primary definition statement was inspected.
Weak-2 was encountered in survey text but was not promoted to a formal DEF record in this session.
next_actions: Prioritize original/primary Schnorr and Kurtz sources; then add weak-n definitions and full strictness graph.

records.area: Martingale, betting, prediction and selection-rule characterizations
records.scope: Monotone martingales, computable/lower-semicomputable betting, non-monotone Kolmogorov-Loveland strategies, selection rules and unpredictability paradigms.
records.why_it_matters: Provides the unpredictability axis and reveals where adaptive/non-monotonic access changes a randomness notion.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: KL definition is currently abstract-inspected rather than proof-inspected; several historical martingale sources remain uncatalogued.
next_actions: Acquire primary martingale characterization sources and inspect KL machinery beyond abstracts.

records.area: Kolmogorov complexity, algorithmic information and incompressibility
records.scope: Plain and prefix-free complexity; coding/incompressibility characterizations; finite-string and infinite-sequence interfaces.
records.why_it_matters: Complexity provides a second foundational characterization axis and is central to lowness, dimension and random-real theory.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Kolmogorov 1965 primary text only metadata-inspected.
Primary Levin/Schnorr sources for the prefix-free characterization have not yet been separately catalogued.
next_actions: Inspect primary complexity definitions and original incompressibility-characterization sources; add conditional/monotone variants only where randomness-relevant.

records.scope: Constructive/effective Hausdorff dimension, supergales, complexity-rate characterizations and finite-string dimension.
records.why_it_matters: Quantifies degrees of algorithmic information/randomness rather than only binary pass/fail notions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Exact supergale definition not statement-inspected, so no DEF record yet.
next_actions: Inspect primary definitions and distinguish constructive dimension, strong dimension and resource-bounded variants.

records.scope: Relativized tests/complexity/betting notions; oracle dependence; van Lambalgen-type phenomena; relative random reals.
records.why_it_matters: Relativization is structurally central to lowness, bases, jumps and higher notions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: No standalone formal DEF record for relative ML randomness yet.
Van Lambalgen 1987 was catalogued only at abstract level; its major theorem was not statement-inspected.
next_actions: Inspect exact relativized definitions and theorems, including van Lambalgen's theorem and oracle-level conventions.

records.area: Lowness notions and bases for randomness
records.scope: Low-for-randomness classes, K-triviality, bases for randomness, traceability interfaces and computational weakness.
records.why_it_matters: Shows how oracles interact with randomness and supplies equivalence classes connecting complexity and relative randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Only a small core equivalence set is indexed; Schnorr/computable lowness and traceability families remain to map.
next_actions: Expand lowness/bases graph with exact primary statements and separations across randomness notions.

records.scope: 2-randomness, n-randomness, weak-2 comparisons, Demuth randomness and other stronger effective-test notions.
records.why_it_matters: Tests the effect of stronger resources and is necessary for an honest implication/separation map.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Demuth original sources not yet acquired/inspected.
Several modern stronger notions have not yet been searched in P1-S001.
next_actions: Build a dedicated stronger-notions tranche with exact definitions, implication chains and separations.

records.scope: Δ1_1-, Π1_1-Martin-Löf-, Π1_1-randomness, higher weak-2/difference notions and lowness at higher levels.
records.why_it_matters: Tests which classical randomness structures persist under higher computability and where genuinely different phenomena arise.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Cambridge chapter full text access restricted; no higher-randomness definition is yet promoted to DEF.
next_actions: Retrieve accessible primary papers and index exact higher definitions/separations.

records.scope: Preservation under effective measure-preserving maps; existence of random preimages; notion-specific failures and maximality principles.
records.why_it_matters: Supplies structural invariance principles that can distinguish randomness notions independently of their syntactic definitions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S001 indexed abstract-level results only; predecessor results attributed to Shen and related conservation literature still need primary-source tracing.
next_actions: Trace primary antecedents, inspect exact map hypotheses, and connect conservation/NRFN records to generalized spaces.

records.area: Computable probability spaces and randomness beyond Cantor space
records.scope: Computable metric/probability spaces, arbitrary computable measures, uniform tests, isomorphisms and non-binary domains.
records.why_it_matters: Prevents the programme from mistaking Cantor-space presentation choices for intrinsic features of randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Current corpus concentrates on Martin-Löf/Schnorr generalizations; other spaces/measures and representation choices remain unmapped.
next_actions: Expand to biased measures, general represented probability spaces and invariance/isomorphism results.

records.scope: Typicality, effective ergodic theorems, mixing computable dynamics and probability-theoretic characterizations tied to individual randomness.
records.why_it_matters: Connects individual randomness to long-run statistical behavior under dynamical systems.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Only one core Schnorr/typicality result is indexed; Martin-Löf and other effective-ergodic characterizations remain untouched.
next_actions: Acquire primary effective Birkhoff/ergodic characterization literature.

records.area: Finite strings, random reals, left-c.e. reals and Ω
records.scope: Randomness/patternlessness for finite strings; infinite reals as binary sequences; left-c.e. random reals; Chaitin Ω and related representations.
records.why_it_matters: Clarifies object type and prevents conflating finite incompressibility with infinite-sequence randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: No dedicated Ω/left-c.e. primary source record yet; finite-string randomness definitions not yet normalized.
next_actions: Add left-c.e./Ω literature and separate finite-string criteria from infinite-sequence notions.

records.area: Pseudorandomness, resource-bounded randomness and derandomization boundary
records.scope: Computational indistinguishability, resource-bounded betting/measure/dimension and derandomization only to clarify contrast with 'genuine' individual randomness.
records.why_it_matters: Needed to distinguish algorithmic randomness of individuals from bounded-observer pseudorandomness without allowing Phase 1 to drift into general complexity theory.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Deliberately deferred in this first foundational session.
next_actions: Later acquire a small boundary corpus sufficient to state distinctions and vocabulary, not an exhaustive derandomization survey.

records.scope: Chance vs individual randomness; statistical typicality vs unpredictability vs incompressibility; only arguments that materially shape mathematical definitions.
records.why_it_matters: Provides conceptual provenance for why different formal frameworks exist, while avoiding nontechnical philosophical sprawl.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: No dedicated philosophy-of-probability literature was collected because P1-S001 prioritizes mathematical definitions/results.
next_actions: Add only sources that resolve terminology/provenance or materially explain formal design choices.

records.scope: Implications, strict implications, equivalences, incomparabilities, relativized relationships and known separations among indexed notions.
records.why_it_matters: A future agent must be able to traverse what a notion implies and what implies it without guessing from definitions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Current relation map is intentionally sparse and source-backed; no inferred edges were added merely because definitions look stronger/weaker.
next_actions: Expand only with exact hypotheses/directions and create explicit incomparability/separation witnesses where source-supported.

records.area: Effective category, genericity and non-measure alternative frameworks
records.scope: Category-based smallness/genericity and other mathematically established alternatives that illuminate the boundary of 'randomness' versus genericity.
records.why_it_matters: The project charter includes measure/category interfaces; understanding nearby non-measure notions prevents conflation of randomness and genericity.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: No dedicated effective-category source search was performed in P1-S001.
next_actions: Acquire a bounded category/genericity corpus and state distinctions from measure-based randomness.
